title: The FSD modules are written against one recovery schema and one login and carry no per-service ownership
source: 03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6
description: Every module of the family states the single `recovery` schema, the `recovery_svc` login and the monolith API base `/api/recovery/v1` as its own, and none of the 19 files names the service, schema or contract that owns a given table, endpoint or event. Version 7 adds a Service line and one Architecture v5 note per module and states that the Microservice Ownership Map v1 is the owner of record, but it does not restate ownership section by section: that is new work for the paired TSD set and the story set, not for this document family.
evidence: FSD P1 v3 'V0001__recovery_schema.sql' and the `recovery.v_ace_*` constraint; FSD P3 v4 `recovery.party_ext`, `recovery.account_ext`; FSD P2 v3 `recovery.v_ace_*`; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-01, DP-02 and DP-13; ADR-013 and ADR-014 (one schema and one login per service); Microservice Ownership Map v1 Tables, Endpoints and Events sheets
proposed: The paired TSD set (Technical Specifications by Module v6, section T0) carries the per-service ownership in buildable form; the FSD family is re-sectioned at the next requirements baseline if the business wants ownership in the functional text. No owner is invented here: the Ownership Map v1 is cited instead.

title: Seven module specifications still send extracts and copies to a data lake that Architecture v5 removes
source: 03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6
section: A1.1 Scope; A1.5; A2 features; ACs
description: FSD P1 carries FEAT-RDF-20 'Copy the decision log to the lake', FSD P7 carries FEAT-DRI-06 'Stream the decision log to the data lake', FSD P2 carries INT-19 and INT-20 as outbound files to the data lake and COLLINS through the data lake, and FSD P4, P6, P9 and P10 name the data lake copy in requirements, integration points and ACs. Architecture v5 has no data lake: reporting reads events into `rwb-reporting` (DP-17, ADR-018), and Template and Rules R6 retires RWB-E1-014. Version 7 keeps every extract and AC word for word and records the position in the Architecture v5 note of each affected module.
evidence: FSD P1 v3 FEAT-RDF-20; FSD P7 v3 FEAT-DRI-06; FSD P2 v3 A1.5 INT-19 and INT-20 and 'In scope'; FSD P6 v3 'Integration points. Power BI, Data lake'; FSD P9 v3 'Integration points. Power BI, Data lake'; FSD P4 v3 REQ-ACA-006; FSD P10 v3 AC-EXC-P10-006-01; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-17, R6 retired row RWB-E1-014; ADR-018
proposed: The data-lake extracts and their ACs are removed at the next FSD baseline and replaced by the event-fed `rwb-reporting` read model; until then the notes and the story set carry the position, and no story builds a lake copy.

title: Five module specifications name the Quartz scheduler as their scheduling mechanism
source: 03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6
description: FSD P3, S1, S4 and S8 give 'Workbench, Quartz scheduler' as their integration points, and FSD P7 carries AC-EXC-P7-014-01, which adds a Quartz job JOB-12. Architecture v5 replaces Quartz with Temporal Schedules and event-started workflows through the workflow kit (DP-10, ADR-016), and Template and Rules R6 retires RWB-TE-007. Version 7 keeps the wording word for word and records the position in the Architecture v5 note of each affected module.
evidence: FSD P3 v4, S1 v3, S4 v3 and S8 v3 'Integration points. Workbench, Quartz scheduler'; FSD P7 v3 AC-EXC-P7-014-01 (Quartz job JOB-12); Template and Rules R5.5 DP-10 and R6 retired row RWB-TE-007; ADR-016
proposed: At the next FSD baseline the Quartz integration points and the JOB-12 AC become Temporal Schedules and event-started workflows on the owning service's task queue; the story set already builds the schedules through RWB-PLT-E1071.
